newsitem.title: CHINA: First Auto first-half net up 59 pct.
newsitem.headline: First Auto first-half net up 59 pct.

text.p: Big Chinese automaker First Automobile Works Car Co Ltd said on Friday its net profits surged 59 percent in the first half of the year, reflecting lower costs and higher value sales.
But the newly listed company did not say how many cars it sold during the period or exactly where it was saving money.
Other automakers in China have complained of sluggish sales, falling prices and mounting competition in the industry.
First Auto's net profits rose to 219.64 million yuan ($26.5 million) in the first half of this year from 138.37 million yuan in the year-ago period.
The company, based in Changchun, capital of northeastern Jilin province, listed 270 million A shares for domestic investors on the southern bourse of Shenzhen in June.
First Auto did not say whether interest on the two billion yuan offer might have contributed to profits or whether the funds had enabled it pay off debt.
First Auto has a joint venture with Volkswagen AG that produces Jetta cars and uses technology from Volkswagen's Audi arm to manufacture the Hongqi (Red Flag) sedan.
Proceeds from the stock offer would be used to expand production of its Red Flag sedan, once exclusively designed for China's communist leaders.
First Auto says it has capacity to produce 30,000 Red Flag cars a year and that the car's domestic content rate stands at 87.5 percent. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
